title.en: Using AI: Can We Trust AI?

narrative_brief: Mini PechaKucha for Science Communication (SDG 9 × AI Literacy × Science Communication)

A2.workbook_text: But AI is not always right. Sometimes it makes fake references, fake papers, and fake facts. This problem is called AI hallucination. It sounds true, but it is not real.

B1.text: However, AI is not always correct. Sometimes it produces fake references, fake papers and fake facts. Researchers call this problem AI hallucination, because the answer sounds true but is not real.
B1.basis: Original B1 kept, except the four slides that pushed the mission above the B1 band (FK 12.2). Facts unchanged.
B1.workbook_text: However, AI is far from perfect and can produce highly misleading errors. Sometimes it creates fake references, fake research papers, or even fake scientific facts. This problem is called AI hallucination.

B2.text: Nevertheless, this powerful technology is far from flawless and can generate problematic errors. A prime example is "AI hallucination," a phenomenon where the algorithm confidently fabricates deceptive data, nonexistent citations, and false scientific assertions that appear entirely authentic.

source_notes.keywords_zh: AI 論文與數據的「幻覺」限制

A2.text: Why does this happen? A model never studies science, and it copies the habits of the writing on the Internet. It only offers the word that usually comes next.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
A2.basis: Full rewrite. Technical corrections: the workbook A2 says AI 'only guesses the next word' and that 'sometimes the formulas and data are completely wrong'. A language model predicts the most likely next word from patterns in the text it was trained on, and what it fabricates is sources, not arithmetic, so those lines are restated as prediction and as invented sources. Nothing here says the model knows, understands or looks anything up.
A2.workbook_text: Why does this happen? AI does not think like people, and it does not truly understand science. It only guesses the next word by using many examples from the Internet.

B1.text: To understand why this happens, remember that AI has no real scientific understanding. It simply runs on math formulas that predict the next word from patterns found across the internet.
B1.basis: Original B1 kept, except the four slides that pushed the mission above the B1 band (FK 12.2). Facts unchanged.
B1.workbook_text: To understand why this happens, we must realize that AI does not possess human intelligence or scientific understanding. Instead, it operates on complex math formulas to predict the next word based on patterns from the internet.

B2.text: Why does this happen? Large language models do not truly understand science. Instead, they generate responses by predicting the most probable sequence of words based on patterns learned from enormous amounts of text.

source_notes.communication_purpose: Explain the scientific principle behind the problem.
source_notes.keywords_zh: 大型語言模型的機率預測本質

A2.text: So the answer can sound perfect and still be wrong. The model never opens a journal or a textbook. Smooth English is simply not the same as truth.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate

A2.workbook_text: Because AI guesses words instead of checking facts, it can give answers that sound correct. But sometimes the formulas and data are completely wrong. This is how AI hallucination happens.

B1.text: These models care more about probability than truth, so they often produce sentences that sound professional. Unfortunately, the data and the papers behind them are sometimes invented by the computer.
B1.basis: Original B1 kept, except the four slides that pushed the mission above the B1 band (FK 12.2). Facts unchanged.
B1.workbook_text: Because these models care more about math probabilities than actual truth, they often create sentences that sound very professional. Unfortunately, the background data and scientific papers are often completely made up by the computer.

B2.text: Because AI predicts language rather than verifying evidence, it may produce information that appears logical and convincing but is factually incorrect. Fluency should never be confused with accuracy.

title.zh: 提出 AI 素養策略與解方

A2.text: So what can we do? First, never treat an AI answer as the final word. Stop for a moment, and ask a simple question: is this really true?
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate

Technical corrections: the workbook A2 says AI 'only guesses the next word' and that 'sometimes the formulas and data are completely wrong'. A language model predicts the most likely next word from patterns in the text it was trained on, and what it fabricates is sources, not arithmetic, so those lines are restated as prediction and as invented sources. Nothing here says the model knows, understands or looks anything up.
A2.workbook_text: So, what should we do? First, do not believe every AI answer immediately. Stop, think, and ask yourself, “Is this really true?” Always check the scientific information first.

B1.text: Therefore, we need critical thinking whenever we work with AI tools. Instead of accepting an answer immediately, we should pause for a moment and check whether the data is real.
B1.basis: Original B1 kept, except the four slides that pushed the mission above the B1 band (FK 12.2). Facts unchanged.
B1.workbook_text: Therefore, we need to use our critical thinking when we work with AI technologies. Instead of accepting the answers immediately, we must take a moment to pause and check if the data is real.

B2.text: So, what should responsible scientists do? First, treat every AI-generated response as a starting point rather than a final answer. Verification should always come before acceptance.

B1.text: In this high-tech world, our unique human voice is still very important. Computers can organize a lot of information, but they do not have human scientific curiosity, natural intuition, or honest hearts.

A2.text: AI is one famous invention of SDG 9. But a clever tool without honest people is just a factory of lies. Machines arrange the words, and we find the truth.
